Spider-man (2002)

Spider-Man (2002) is a landmark superhero film directed by Sam Raimi, chronicling the origin of Peter Parker (Tobey Maguire), a shy high schooler who gains spider-like powers after a genetic experiment bite. Set in NYC, the film focuses on his journey to fight crime as Spider-Man while tackling personal drama and the menacing Green Goblin (Willem Dafoe).

source_details.synopsis: Spider-Man is a 2002 American superhero film directed by Sam Raimi and written by David Koepp. Based on the Marvel Comics character Spider-Man, it is the first film in Raimi's Spider-Man trilogy (2002–2007), and stars Tobey Maguire, Willem Dafoe, Kirsten Dunst, James Franco, Cliff Robertson, and Rosemary Harris. The plot follows the timid teenager Peter Parker (Maguire), who gains superhuman abilities after being bitten by a genetically engineered spider. He adopts the masked persona "Spider-Man" and begins to fight crime in New York City, facing the malevolent Green Goblin (Dafoe) in the process.
